overview: Two beta-hemolytic streptococci separated by Lancefield grouping and, most importantly, by which patients they threaten.
genZNote: Group A or Group B — one bacitracin disk tells you which.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Group A Streptococcus (GAS), a beta-hemolytic strep responsible for pharyngitis and invasive skin infections.
aspects.valueB: Group B Streptococcus (GBS), a beta-hemolytic strep best known as a cause of neonatal sepsis.

aspects.label: Hemolysis
aspects.valueB: Beta-hemolytic (typically narrower zone than Group A).

aspects.label: Key Population at Risk
aspects.valueA: School-age children (pharyngitis), any age (skin/soft tissue, invasive disease).
aspects.valueB: Neonates (via vertical transmission during delivery) and pregnant women.

aspects.label: Relevant Screening/Identification Test
aspects.valueA: Bacitracin sensitivity (sensitive) helps distinguish it from Group B.
aspects.valueB: CAMP test positive and bacitracin-resistant; routine antenatal rectovaginal screening at 35–37 weeks.

aspects.label: Disease Spectrum
aspects.valueA: Pharyngitis, impetigo, cellulitis, necrotizing fasciitis, toxic shock, post-strep sequelae (rheumatic fever, glomerulonephritis).
aspects.valueB: Neonatal sepsis/meningitis, chorioamnionitis, and postpartum infections; occasionally invasive disease in adults with comorbidities.

aspects.label: Prevention Strategy
aspects.valueA: No routine antenatal screening; treatment is reactive to symptomatic infection.
aspects.valueB: Universal antenatal screening with intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis for colonized mothers.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Group A, bacitracin-sensitive, linked to post-infectious sequelae.
aspects.valueB: Group B, CAMP-positive, linked to neonatal disease and antenatal screening.
